seo_description: Solo audio designer on a 4-player racing game. Procedural MetaSounds engine, priority-based mix for 4 players, and full audio pipeline in 12 weeks.
hero.title: Not Today, Darling!
hero.subtitle: Solo Audio Designer / 4-player side-scrolling racer / 12 weeks
concept.hook: Solo audio designer. 4 players racing at once. 12 weeks to ship everything from scratch.
concept.p1: Not Today, Darling! is a chaotic 4-player side-scrolling racer where grannies smash and scream their way to victory. Power-ups fire alongside collisions, character voices, engine sounds. The mix had to stay readable under that kind of pressure.
concept.p2: I was the only audio person on the 8-person team. Everything went through me: procedural go-kart engine in MetaSounds, surface-reactive driving sounds, a priority-based Sound Class mix for 4 simultaneous players, and character voice recording with the team.
systems.engine.title: Procedural Go-Kart Engine
systems.engine.desc: Built in MetaSounds. RPM, throttle, and load drive the engine sound in real-time with no baked loops. It responds to player input frame by frame, so the engine feels physically connected to the kart.
systems.mix.title: Priority-Based Mix
systems.mix.desc: 4 players means 4 engines, 4 sets of power-ups, collisions, and voices going simultaneously. Sound Classes with priority levels keep the local player's audio on top. Attenuation presets push distant karts into the background. Without it, the mix turns to mud.
systems.voices.title: Character Voices
systems.voices.desc: We recorded granny voice lines with the team: reactions to collisions, power-ups, overtakes. Implemented as randomized Sound Cues with cooldown timers so they don't spam.
challenge1.title: Mix Clarity with 4 Players
challenge1.hard: 4 karts, 4 engines, power-ups and collisions all playing at once on top of character voices. Without management, everything collapsed into noise. Players couldn't tell what was happening to their own kart.
challenge1.did: Built a Sound Class hierarchy with priority levels. The local player's kart always sits on top of the mix. Distant karts get attenuated and ducked. Power-up and collision sounds run through concurrency limits, so only the most relevant ones play.
challenge2.title: Procedural Engine That Feels Right
challenge2.hard: MetaSounds procedural synthesis can sound sterile and disconnected from what's on screen. The engine had to respond instantly to throttle changes and actually feel like it's powering the kart.
challenge2.did: Mapped RPM, throttle position, and load directly to MetaSounds parameters. Added pitch smoothing so sudden input changes don't cause jarring jumps. The result tracks player input frame by frame.
